basis: Only NPS-documented dock, named trail, boardwalk, campsite or day-trail relationships. No calculated trail geometry, campsite availability, docking clearance or return service.

rows.title: Presque Isle: boardwalk to site 1
stages: Arrive only if the west Presque Isle public dock is usable and your transport is confirmed.
Use the NPS-documented boardwalk from the west-side harbor dock to accessible campsite 1 and nearby facilities.
Confirm site 1 permit separately; check the return crossing with your operator.
rows.caution: The campsite path is documented; the water approach, docking and reservation are not verified here.

rows.title: Presque Isle: shoreline campground
rows.routeLabel: NPS campsite locations along Presque Isle Bay
stages: Arrive at Presque Isle only with a confirmed vessel and dock plan.
NPS places campsites 2–19 along about three-quarters of a mile of Presque Isle Bay shoreline; site 2 is nearest the dock.
Use the official campground map and signs to locate your assigned site; arrange return transport.
rows.caution: NPS does not name a continuous dock-to-site trail for every campsite. Erosion has removed direct beach access at many sites; no straight-line approach is shown.

rows.title: Quarry Bay: accessible group camps A and B
stages: Verify your boat's approach and public Quarry Bay dock access.
Follow the NPS boardwalk from the Quarry Bay dock to group campsite A or B.
Confirm the specific group reservation, printed permit and return trip.
rows.caution: These are group sites, not individual campsite substitutes. The former inter-bay bridge washout means no unverified overland route between Quarry and Presque Isle.

rows.title: Quarry Bay: individual site 20
rows.routeLabel: NPS describes site 20 as ¼ mile west of dock
stages: Check the public Quarry Bay dock and independent vessel return plan.
NPS locates site 20 about one-quarter mile west of the dock, in trees behind the west end of the beach.
Confirm the site permit and local wayfinding; no traced footpath has been inferred.
rows.caution: A published site location is not a mapped trail alignment. Do not substitute the nearby beach for guaranteed landing access.

rows.title: Julian Bay beach walk
stages: Arrive at the Presque Isle visitor area using authorized water transport.
Walk the NPS Julian Bay Trail from the ranger station to the beach.
Return to the dock on your confirmed transport schedule.
rows.caution: This is a day-hike relationship, not a campsite route. The 0.4-mile published trail length does not include transport or other walking.

rows.title: Oak: campsites nearest the west dock
stages: Confirm transport to the NPS west public dock.
NPS locates individual site 2 about 0.1 mile west, site 3 about 0.25 mile west and group B about 50 yards west of the dock.
Locate your assigned campsite using the NPS map and check the permit and pickup.
rows.caution: These are NPS descriptive distances, not a drawn trail. Group B is a group-permit site.

rows.title: Oak: sandspit campsites 1 and A
rows.routeLabel: Sandspit Trail · NPS describes 1.5 miles from dock
stages: Confirm west dock landing and an actual return boat.
Follow the NPS Sandspit Trail toward the southern sandspit.
Locate individual site 1 or group A on the designated sandspit area; use only established paths, boardwalks or beach.
rows.caution: Sandspit vegetation is fragile. Group site A requires a group reservation. Dock-to-sandspit distance comes from the NPS campsite description.

rows.title: Oak: Northwest Beach campsite 4
rows.routeLabel: Northwest Beach Trail via Loop Trail
stages: Confirm landing at the west dock and assess the longer backcountry day.
Take the NPS Loop Trail to the Northwest Beach Trail junction, then follow that named trail toward campsite 4.
Verify campsite allocation, daylight and the return route before leaving the dock area.
rows.caution: NPS trail and campsite pages give slightly different dock-to-site distances (about 2.8 and 3 miles). No exact total or route geometry is inferred.

rows.title: Oak: North Bay campsite 6
rows.routeLabel: North Bay Trail via Loop Trail
stages: Confirm west dock access and allow for a longer overland approach.
Follow NPS Loop Trail connections to the North Bay Trail and campsite 6.
Verify site-specific conditions and how you will leave the island.
rows.caution: NPS descriptions differ slightly on dock-to-site distance (about 3.7 and 4 miles). This guide does not resolve that into a false precise estimate.

rows.title: Oak: high overlook hike
stages: Arrive at the west dock with a scheduled return plan.
Follow the inland Loop Trail to the signed Overlook Trail junction.
Enjoy the view and return by the documented trail network in time for your confirmed boat.
rows.caution: NPS describes the overlook roughly 3.5 miles from the dock. This is a trail outing, not a shortcut to a campsite.

rows.title: Sand: accessible site 3 and group C
stages: Check East Bay public dock access with your operator.
Use the NPS boardwalk to accessible site 3 or group C (NPS lists them near the dock).
Verify campsite permit and return transport independently.
rows.caution: NPS is correcting Sand Island campsite coordinates. These connections are documented in prose but no campsite pins are plotted.

rows.title: Sand: Wellisch Cabin Trail camps
stages: Land only if the East Bay dock and transport are confirmed.
Follow the Wellisch Cabin Trail south from East Bay dock, passing site 2 and group sites A and B.
Find the assigned site from current NPS signs; arrange an independent return.
rows.caution: No Sand campsite coordinates are plotted while NPS corrects its published table. A/B require group camping permits.

rows.title: Sand: lighthouse approach and site 6
rows.routeLabel: Lighthouse Trail · NPS lists site 6 about 1 mile north
stages: Arrive at the NPS East Bay dock with confirmed transport.
Take the Lighthouse Trail north; NPS locates site 6 on the east side about a mile from the dock.
Use the official map and signs for the site, then confirm permit and return.
rows.caution: Site 6 has a separate toilet approach; NPS says there is no direct campsite-to-toilet path. Site coordinate withheld pending corrections.

rows.title: Sand: lighthouse day walk
stages: Confirm East Bay dock access and return pickup.
Take the NPS Lighthouse Trail north from the dock toward the lighthouse.
Return using the original mapped trail, allowing for conditions and the actual boat schedule.
rows.caution: The boardwalk may be slippery when wet. This is not an endorsement of landing at Lighthouse Bay or reaching campsites 4/5.

rows.title: Rocky: north shore campsites 4, 5 and A
stages: Verify use of the east public dock.
From the dock bulletin board take the NPS North Trail, which passes sites 4, 5 and group A.
Check the assigned permit and turn back before private land beyond group A.
rows.caution: The 0.45 mile is the trail's published length, not a measured dock-to-each-site distance. Respect the private-property boundary.

rows.title: Rocky: sites 2 and 3 near the dock
stages: Confirm east dock access for the actual date.
NPS describes sites 2 and 3 within about a quarter mile of the dock, reached on short walks.
Find the marked campsite; do not assume the rocky beach is a safe or adequate small-boat landing.
rows.caution: NPS does not specify a named trail connection to sites 2 and 3. No trail line is drawn.

rows.title: Basswood: dock-side campsites A, 5 and 6
rows.routeLabel: Short right branch at dock clearing
stages: Verify the west dock and carry gear uphill to the clearing.
At the island trail junction follow the NPS-described short right-hand branch through group A toward sites 5 and 6.
Confirm the assigned site and separate return transport.
rows.caution: NPS locates the group site roughly 200 yards south of dock; this is a short campsite branch, not the full 5.5-mile farm-and-quarry loop.

rows.title: Basswood: farm and quarry loop
stages: Confirm west dock and a realistic return vessel plan.
Start at the clearing uphill from dock and follow the NPS trail loop by the historic farm and brownstone quarry.
Return to dock via the marked loop and verify conditions before setting out.
rows.caution: NPS describes sites 1–4 southwest of the quarry but does not establish a precise branch from the loop to each campsite. This is not a campsite-access line.

rows.title: Michigan: sandspit campsite 1
stages: Confirm an actual landing at the Michigan Island light station; passing lighthouse cruises may not stop.
From behind the light station near the vault toilet take the NPS Sandspit / Campsite Trail toward site 1.
Camp only in the designated site behind the dunes; confirm permit and boat pickup.
rows.caution: NPS campsite description places the site about 0.9 mile west of light station; trail directory lists a 1.0-mile route. No exact dock-to-site mileage is calculated.

rows.title: Raspberry: lighthouse and island trails
rows.routeLabel: West Bay Trail and Sandspit Trail
stages: Confirm the operator's actual landing and departure time at Raspberry light station.
Explore the NPS West Bay or Sandspit hiking trails from lighthouse grounds.
Return to the boat. There are no designated campsites or primitive camping on Raspberry.
rows.caution: This is a day-only experience; a published tour listing does not guarantee a landing.

rows.title: Devils: closed south harbor
stages: Do not plan a dock landing or an overnight stay at the south marina from the historical NPS map.
Read the current NPS construction and park conditions notices.
Choose another island if you need a permitted landing, overnight stay, or campsite.
rows.caution: Closed in the reviewed NPS construction record; this guide does not infer a reopening or recommend alternate rock landings.
